summary: Parameter tensor coherence over arbitrary modules: native associator and both unitors, their horizontal inverses and a concrete affine-line parameter test, retaining the full general ringed-site plan and every source route. The codex-a71f92 common-λ affine exterior continuation constructs the actual balanced degree-one extension, proves its scalar correction and the exact curvature defect λ(e⊗d₀λ∧d₀a), computes unit curvature, and proves the full common-λ tensor-curvature formula and factor-flatness implication for arbitrary modules. No constant-λ assumption is used in the raw tensor-curvature equation. All 149 routed obligations, the reserved general finite-locally-free ringed-site key, E1 tensor/exterior restriction, equality detection/gluing, cross-ring exterior/curvature transport, arbitrary-Q tensor-valued shuffle, determinant/Tate/period adapters and H.1–H.8 remain open. Earlier narrower frontier paragraphs are preserved checkpoint history. Actual affine degree-one extension and curvature now commute with horizontal maps. Module-equivalence conjugation preserves the parameter, composes, has an inverse and transports flatness; curvatureLinear packages the constant-parameter curvature and its tensor formula as native R-linear maps. The ℤ[x] shear test retains the nonzero −2 frame derivative. Global sheaf descent/restriction/equality detection, ring-changing exterior transport, all five supplier requests,149 routed source items and H.1–H.8 remain open. Coefficient-ring transport continuation: 21 nodes and14 typed tests on actual semilinear calculus maps, identity/composition, horizontal extension/curvature and explicit flatness detection. Every inherited scope and global gap remains.

nodes.title: Commuting coordinate directions with constant parameter
nodes.statement: Frame consists of d k-linear derivations δ_i:R→R, pairwise commuting on every a∈R, with δ_i(λ)=0. This is a specified affine frame, not a definition of a general differential site.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
proofSteps: Use the pinned Derivation carrier and record its pairwise commutation and constant-parameter equations.
Zero derivations give Frame.zero. On k[X_0,…,X_(d−1)], partial derivatives give Frame.polynomial with constant parameter C(c).
Prove polynomial commutation on monomials: successive removal of i,j has the same coefficient in both orders, including i=j; extend by k-linearity. Constants differentiate to zero.
Frame.one keeps the directions and uses δ_i(1)=0. No invertibility of λ is assumed.
acceptance: λ=X_0 with δ_0=∂_0 is excluded over Q since δ_0λ=1.
Zero directions are allowed, but are not universal differential forms.

nodes.title: Coordinate change by an invertible matrix
nodes.statement: For a matrix unit G and the convention s′=Gs, define A′_i=G A_i G^−1−λδ_i(G)G^−1. The associated operator is G D_i G^−1 on the new component column.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.

proofSteps: Differentiate G G^−1=I to get δ_i(G^−1)=−G^−1δ_i(G)G^−1.
Expand G D_i(G^−1s′): its derivative coefficient is λ and its matrix coefficient has the displayed minus sign.
Its operator commutator is G[D_i,D_j]G^−1. Use the commutator node and coordinate basis evaluation to identify κ′_ij=Gκ_ijG^−1.
Invertibility of G proves preservation and reflection of curvature vanishing.
acceptance: The fixed convention is s′=Gs; the opposite convention changes the formula.
Gauge of zero matrices need not have zero matrices when λδG≠0.

nodes.title: Tensor with the same parameter
nodes.statement: For models c on R^V and b on R^W with the same F and λ, construct the free model on R^(V×W) with matrices A_i⊗I_W+I_V⊗B_i, using the Kronecker product. Its parameter is λ, not 2λ.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.
Matrix products and scalar actions are over R, on the free coordinate module R^V.
proofSteps: Use the standard free-coordinate tensor identification and define the Kronecker sum.
Entrywise differentiate; the cross commutators cancel since A⊗I commutes with I⊗B. The remaining curvature is κ_c⊗I+I⊗κ_b.
On elementary tensors, λδ(s⊗t)=λδ(s)⊗t+s⊗λδ(t). Scalar balancing identifies the derivative term represented in either factor, so one λ occurs.
Vanishing of both input curvatures implies vanishing of the tensor curvature; no converse is claimed.
acceptance: Input parameters must agree.
The balanced tensor scalar Leibniz rule has one λ derivative term.

d∈N, λ∈R, F is a commuting constant-parameter Frame, and V is a finite decidable index type.

proofSteps: Differentiate u u^−1=1 and use δ_i(u)=0 to obtain δ_i(u^−1)=0.

Invertibility makes flatness equivalent. Merely changing λ's type while leaving A unscaled is incorrect.
acceptance: Over Q[X], the zero-matrix λ=2 model maps X to 2; rescaling maps X to 1.
λ=0 and nonunit parameters do not admit this operation.

hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.

Zero matrices satisfy bound 1; one-letter words show that bound 1 iff every A_i=0.

nodes.title: Intrinsic parameter preconnections
nodes.statement: A Preconnection(E,λ) is an additive map of sheaves D:E→E⊗_OΩ¹ satisfying D(ae)=aD(e)+λ(e⊗da) on every object after local restriction. It is not O-linear unless its Leibniz correction vanishes. Integrability is a separate predicate; neither a lattice nor trace-zero nor nilpotence is part of this carrier.
hypotheses: A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition.
λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object.

Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.
proofSteps: Use the native module-sheaf carrier and imported sheaf tensor. Define D as a morphism of underlying abelian sheaves.
Impose the displayed local Leibniz equality, compatible with all restrictions. This automatically gives linearity over the relatively constant base.
Equality of D as an additive sheaf map gives equality of preconnections; construction requires actual data and the equality, not a supplied unnamed proposition.

nodes.title: Tensor nilpotence and finite filtrations
nodes.statement: When Q is finite locally free, θ^[N]=0 for N>0 iff a length-N nilpotence filtration exists. No integrability is needed for this equivalence of ordered iterates and lowering filtrations. For a general coherent Q without flatness, this equivalence is not asserted.
hypotheses: A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition.
λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object.

Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.
Q=Ω¹⊗T is finite locally free; E finite locally free, and the tensor-exactness/kernel identification for Q is imported from E1.
proofSteps: A lowering filtration kills N successive applications on E=K_N.
Conversely define K_j=ker θ^[j]. Locally a finite basis of Q identifies K_j with vectors annihilated by all words of length j.
These kernels ascend and θ(K_j)⊆K_{j−1}⊗Q: contraction by each basis covector lands in K_{j−1}; finite locally free tensor exactness identifies the kernel after tensoring.
K_0=ker id=0 and θ^[N]=0 gives K_N=E; glue kernels without asserting they or their quotients are locally free.

nodes.title: Tensor nilpotence bound
nodes.statement: If two same-Q fields have positive ordered bounds N and M, their tensor field has bound N+M−1. The proof is valid in arbitrary characteristic and over nonreduced rings, without dividing by binomial coefficients.
hypotheses: A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O) with a specified relative exterior differential calculus Ω⁰=O, Ωⁿ=∧ⁿ_O Ω¹, restriction-compatible wedge and additive relative differentials d; d²=0 and the graded Leibniz identity hold. No smoothness, field, characteristic-zero or reducedness premise is built into the connection definition.
λ is a global central O-section with dλ=0. E is a finite locally free O-module sheaf; rank is only locally constant, and a local trivialization is never part of the object.

Tensor products here are sheaf tensor products; elementary-section formulas are verified locally and glued. Tensor of global section modules is not identified with global sections of the sheaf tensor.
proofSteps: Expand the (N+M−1)-fold iterate as a sum indexed by choosing the E or F action at every position; distributivity and tensor associators give this formula without a basis of Q.

Reorder actions on separate E,F factors while retaining the corresponding permutation of the ordered Q factors. Every summand factors through an E iterate of length r and an F iterate of length s with r+s=N+M−1.

Either r≥N or s≥M. Higher iterates factor through the specified zero iterate, so that summand vanishes. This is an integral shuffle argument: no integrability between directions, local freeness of Q or division by binomial coefficients is required.

The contraction adapter supplies the necessary N+M−1 bound after evaluating every slot in the same dual direction, and an integral binomial identity for that specialization. Complete the mixed E/F shuffle factorization before concluding actual ordered-tensor vanishing; self-contraction powers do not detect mixed words in characteristic two.

The mixed contraction-word expansion now yields the actual affine ordered tensor bound with a chosen finite coefficient basis. It covers arbitrary E,F and arbitrary characteristic without integrability. Remove the coefficient-basis restriction via an actual tensor-valued shuffle and discharge native sheaf restriction/gluing before concluding this unchanged general ringed-site theorem.

The actual affine ordered tensor bound N+M−1 now extends from finite-basis coefficients to finite-projective Q by a native finite free retract, and to principal covers with local projective coefficient data. E and F need not be flat. The general arbitrary-Q tensor-valued shuffle, native finite-projective sheaf restriction/tensor-power coherence, equality detection and gluing remain required. These affine results do not identify tensors of global sections with sheaf tensor sections or close the reserved general ringed-site key.

nodes.title: Griffiths transverse filtrations
nodes.statement: For an ordinary integrable connection (E,∇), a GriffithsFiltration is a bounded decreasing Z-indexed filtration F^pE by subbundles, exhaustive for p≤a and zero for p>b, with finite locally free successive quotients and ∇F^p⊆F^{p−1}⊗Ω¹. Only this filtration-to-graded algebra is defined here; a VHS additionally has the local-system/fibrewise Hodge data supplied by D3.

nodes.title: Associated graded Higgs field

nodes.title: Coordinate determinant parameter connection
nodes.statement: For the finite free coordinate model c with matrices A_i, construct a rank-one coordinate model det(c) with the same F and λ and one-by-one matrix tr(A_i). Its section operator is s ↦ λδ_i(s)+tr(A_i)s. This is the local coefficient model for the induced top exterior-power connection; the global determinant sheaf, the wedge identification and change-of-frame descent are separate supplier/bridge obligations. Rank zero gives the unit-line connection with zero coefficient.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
F is the existing coordinate Frame: its k-linear derivations commute and annihilate λ. Every coordinate model uses this same frame.
The index types V and W are finite decidable types. No positive rank, characteristic-zero or invertibility of rank is assumed.
proofSteps: Define the rank-one matrices by the existing matrix trace, summing diagonal entries; reuse the existing coordinate Connection carrier with index Fin 1.
The operator formula follows from the existing operator equation. The scalar derivative term has λ, not rank(V)λ; the rank only multiplies scalar coefficient matrices.
This construction uses no scalar division, exterior-sheaf construction or global frame choice. Its identification with a top exterior power is recorded as a separate gap, not an assumed theorem.
acceptance: Distinguish trace(A_i) from the algebraic determinant of A_i.
The model preserves the source parameter at every rank, including rank zero.
Trace loses information: flatness of det(c) has no converse.

Apply AddMonoidHom.map_trace to each derivation, commuting differentiation with the finite diagonal sum. Apply trace_add, trace_sub and trace_smul to the original curvature.
Matrix.trace_mul_comm identifies tr(A_i A_j) and tr(A_j A_i); their difference cancels. No division by rank or by two is used.
acceptance: Valid over any commutative coefficient ring, including characteristic two.

nodes.title: Curvature under coordinate change
nodes.statement: For the coordinate transformation s′=Gs and every invertible matrix G, curvature transforms as κ_gauge(c,G),ij=G κ_c,ij G⁻¹. This is the promoted curvature API of the inherited gauge construction.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
F is the existing coordinate Frame: its k-linear derivations commute and annihilate λ. Every coordinate model uses this same frame.
The index types V and W are finite decidable types. No positive rank, characteristic-zero or invertibility of rank is assumed.
proofSteps: Differentiate GG⁻¹=I entrywise. The matrix product Leibniz rule gives δ_i(G⁻¹)=−G⁻¹δ_i(G)G⁻¹ by multiplying the resulting zero identity on the left by G⁻¹.

Insert the defined coefficient G A_i G⁻¹−λδ_i(G)G⁻¹ into the curvature formula. Use the preceding inverse derivative, the relatively constant parameter and commutation of the coordinate derivations to cancel all terms with derivatives of G; the remaining expression is G(λδ_iA_j−λδ_jA_i+[A_i,A_j])G⁻¹. Finite matrix sums and multiplication are over the commutative ring R.
acceptance: The transformation convention is s′=Gs, so the derivative correction has a minus sign.
No field, characteristic-zero hypothesis or matrix inverse in a field is used: G is a unit of the matrix ring.

nodes.title: Determinant curvature is gauge invariant
nodes.statement: For every invertible coordinate matrix G, the one-by-one curvature entry of det(c.gauge(G)) equals that of det(c).
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
F is the existing coordinate Frame: its k-linear derivations commute and annihilate λ. Every coordinate model uses this same frame.
The index types V and W are finite decidable types. No positive rank, characteristic-zero or invertibility of rank is assumed.
proofSteps: Apply determinant-curvature on both sides and the inherited gauge curvature identity κ_gauge=G κ G⁻¹.
Matrix.trace_units_conj proves equality of the two traces. This requires no derivative of det(G).

This is curvature invariance only; the connection coefficient still has its trace of the derivative correction. A global determinant descent theorem also needs the induced frame det(G) and the Jacobi derivative formula.
acceptance: Do not assert that the determinant connection matrices themselves are unchanged under a nonconstant gauge.

nodes.title: Derivation of a determinant by row replacements
nodes.statement: For a k-linear derivation δ:R→R and any square matrix S, δ(det S)=Σ_r det(updateRow S r (j↦δ(S_rj))). S need not be invertible.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.
proofSteps: Use the pinned det_apply' permutation formula. Additivity moves δ through the finite sum; Derivation.map_intCast kills each integer-valued permutation sign.

Induct over the finite product for each permutation: δ(Π_j S_(σj),j)=Σ_j δ(S_(σj),j) Π_{l≠j} S_(σl),l. The empty product derivative is δ(1)=0. This is an induction using the existing Leibniz rule, not a new generic product carrier.

For a fixed permutation, the row-replacement determinant has exactly one differentiated factor, in the column j=σ⁻¹(r). Reindex the finite row sum r=σ(j), then exchange the permutation and column sums. The permutation sign is unchanged.
No inverse is introduced. The argument also works for singular matrices, repeated rows and characteristic two; do not prove alternating vanishing by cancelling 2.
acceptance: The 0×0 determinant is 1, whose derivative and empty row sum are zero.
For S=diag(x,x) over F₂[x], δ(det S)=δ(x²)=0, and the two replacement terms cancel in characteristic two.
The formula applies to singular matrices; invertibility is added only at the unit Jacobi node.

nodes.title: Trace of infinitesimal left row action
nodes.statement: For square matrices A and S over R, Σ_r det(updateRow S r ((A*S)r)) = tr(A) det(S). S is arbitrary, including singular matrices.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.
proofSteps: Expand (A*S)_r=Σ_j A_rj • S_j using the native matrix multiplication finite sum.

For each fixed replacement row r, use determinant additivity and scalar linearity in that row to move this sum outside: Σ_j A_rj det(updateRow S r S_j). Finite-sum linearity follows by induction from det_updateRow_add and det_updateRow_smul.
If j≠r, the replacement matrix has rows j and r equal, so det_updateRow_eq_zero applies. This native alternating lemma works in characteristic two without dividing by 2.
The only surviving term is j=r, with updateRow S r S_r=S. Sum A_rr det(S) over r and identify the diagonal sum with Matrix.trace. In rank zero both sides vanish.
acceptance: For A=diag(a,b) and S=diag(x,y), the sum is (a+b)xy.
An off-diagonal elementary A has trace zero, and every nonzero candidate replacement term has duplicated rows.
Do not confuse this statement with Tau Ceti's existing column-weight identity sum_det_updateRow_mul_row, whose replacement entries are d_j S_rj, not (A*S)_rj.

nodes.title: Determinant coefficient under coordinate change
nodes.statement: For the inherited convention s′=Gs and frame F, (det(c.gauge G)).matrix_i,0,0 = tr(A_i) − λ det(G⁻¹) δ_i(det G). The determinant connection coefficient is not generally gauge invariant.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.
F is the inherited coordinate frame with commuting derivations annihilating λ; c is an arbitrary, not necessarily flat, connection on that frame.
proofSteps: Apply determinant_matrix to c.gauge G, then the inherited gauge_matrix formula A′_i=G A_i G⁻¹−λ(δ_iG)G⁻¹.
Move trace through subtraction and scalar multiplication using the existing trace_sub and trace_smul declarations; trace_units_conj reduces the first term to tr(A_i).

Import ColemanPowerSeries:L1/derivation-determinant-unit with δ=F.delta i and use the pinned Matrix.trace_mul_comm to match its G⁻¹δG trace orientation. Multiply its identity by det(G⁻¹), using determinant multiplicativity and the matrix-unit inverse law; this logarithmic form converts the trace of the derivative correction into det(G⁻¹)δ_i(det G).
Keep the minus sign dictated by s′=Gs, and retain λ rather than rank·λ. For λ=0 the derivative term vanishes; this is the conjugation-only Higgs specialization.
acceptance: For A=0, λ=1 and G=diag(x,1), the new line coefficient is −x⁻¹, not zero.
For G=diag(x,x⁻¹) the determinant correction vanishes even though the vector connection changes.
An empty vector bundle induces the unit line: det G=1 and the transformed line coefficient remains zero.

nodes.title: Determinant connection commutes with gauge transport
nodes.statement: Let g=Units.map Matrix.detMonoidHom G∈Rˣ, and let ℓ(g)=Units.map (Matrix.scalar (Fin 1)).toMonoidHom g be the native one-by-one matrix unit. Then (c.gauge G).determinant = c.determinant.gauge ℓ(g), with the same F and λ.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.
F is the inherited coordinate frame with commuting derivations annihilating λ; c is an arbitrary, not necessarily flat, connection on that frame.
proofSteps: Build g and ℓ(g) only by the existing native monoid homomorphisms and Units.map. Units.coe_map exposes values det G and scalar(det G); inverse values are det(G⁻¹) and scalar(det(G⁻¹)). No new determinant-line carrier or arbitrary choice is introduced.
Apply the inherited gauge_matrix formula to the one-by-one determinant connection. Its coefficient is (det G) tr(A_i) det(G⁻¹) − λ δ_i(det G)det(G⁻¹).

Use det_mul and the inverse equation to simplify the conjugation scalar product to tr(A_i). Commutativity reorders the derivative factors; determinant-gauge-matrix supplies equality with the left side.

Connections are determined by their matrix field. Extensionality over directions and the unique Fin 1 row and column proves equality of coordinate connection objects. Their operator compatibility then follows from the inherited operator definition.
This is exact finite-coordinate frame coherence. It does not construct exterior-power sheaves or glue local operators; those remain E1/global-comparison obligations.
acceptance: The transformation uses det G, not tr G, and exactly the existing gauge convention.
A nonconstant diagonal Laurent gauge reproduces the negative logarithmic derivative term on both sides.
The rank-zero vector frame maps to the identity one-by-one frame on the unit line.

nodes.title: Alternating determinant evaluation intertwines the section operator
nodes.statement: Represent an ordered family of sections as the rows of S. For each direction i, Σ_r det(updateRow S r (c.operator i (S r))) = c.determinant.operator i (fun _↦det S) 0 = λδ_i(det S)+tr(A_i)det S. No flatness or invertibility of S is assumed.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra.
d∈N and λ∈R; all derivations are k-linear.
V is a finite decidable index type, including the empty type. No domain, field, characteristic-zero, factorial or rank-invertibility hypothesis is used.
F is the inherited coordinate frame with commuting derivations annihilating λ; c is an arbitrary, not necessarily flat, connection on that frame.
proofSteps: Expand each section operator as λδ_i(S_r)+A_i*ᵥS_r. Use determinant linearity in the replaced row to split the derivative and matrix-action sums.
Pull λ out of each derivative replacement using det_updateRow_smul. The determinant-derivation-rows identity reduces that sum to λδ_i(det S).

For any perturbation matrix H, the sum of single-row replacement determinants Σ_r det(updateRow S r H_r) equals the sum of single-column replacement determinants Σ_j det(updateCol S j (r↦H_rj)). Expand det_apply' on both sides: each permutation term replaces exactly one entry S_(σj),j by H_(σj),j, and the row index is reindexed as r=σ(j). No derivation or invertibility is needed for this finite-sum reindexing.

For H_r=A_i*ᵥS_r, entrywise H=S*A_iᵀ, not A_i*S. Convert its replacement-row sum to the preceding replacement-column sum, transpose each determinant, and observe Hᵀ=A_i*Sᵀ. The determinant-row-action node with A_i and Sᵀ now gives tr(A_i)det(Sᵀ)=tr(A_i)det S. This explicitly justifies the column-vector/row-family orientation; duplicate-row vanishing, not cancellation by 2, handles every characteristic.
Apply determinant_operator to identify the resulting scalar with the one-by-one line section operator. The empty family evaluates to det(∅)=1 and both sides are zero because δ_i(1)=0.
This is the local alternating universal-property test needed by a future top-wedge comparison. It is not yet a connection on a global exterior-power module/sheaf.
acceptance: With S=diag(x,y), λ=1, δ=∂x and A=diag(a,b), both sides equal y+(a+b)xy.
For an off-diagonal A, the action part is zero on every S, not merely invertible S.
Rank zero gives the derivative of the unit section, not a zero determinant line.

nodes.title: Contraction of an affine twisted field
nodes.statement: For an A-linear θ:E→E⊗_A Q, construct the A-linear contraction map a_θ:V→End_A(E), a_θ(v)=(E⊗v)θ followed by the right tensor unit equivalence E⊗A≅E. This is the affine section formula of the existing twisted field, not a new Higgs or dual carrier.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed.

V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative.
proofSteps: Use the native tensor map of id_E and v; compose with the native right tensor unit equivalence and θ.
Use native TensorProduct.map_add_right and map_smul_right to prove linearity in the contracting functional, then compose with θ and rid. This actual affine proof works for arbitrary modules.

On local finite projective charts, evaluation separates tensor coefficients. Its sheaf/co-evaluation and gluing interface is the E1 supplier, not an assumption that global sections commute with tensor.

nodes.title: Morphisms intertwine the symmetric action
nodes.statement: For contraction maps a:V→End_A(E), b:V→End_A(F) and their generator-preserving actions α,β, an A-linear f:E→F satisfies f∘a(v)=b(v)∘f for every v iff f∘α(s)=β(s)∘f for every s∈S. For finite locally free Q these equalities identify Higgs-horizontal morphisms with intertwining the actual S-actions.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed.

V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative.
F is another A-module. The action maps on both modules use the same coefficient dual V and the same symmetric algebra S.
proofSteps: An intertwiner of all s intertwines degree-one generators.
For the converse, use native symmetric-algebra induction on scalars, generators, sums and products. A-linearity of f handles scalars; composing the two induction equalities handles products.
On finite local bases, dual evaluation identifies the generator equalities with (f⊗id_Q)θ_E=θ_F f. Restriction and equality of sheaf maps glue; this is not a new module category carrier.

nodes.title: Ordered tensor coefficients detect vanishing
nodes.statement: For every N≥0, an O-linear θ:E→E⊗Q with Q finite locally free has θ^[N]=0 iff every ordered word of N dual contractions vanishes, locally on each coefficient trivializing chart. In a basis θ=Σ_i A_i⊗q_i, the coefficient of q_(i₁)⊗⋯⊗q_(i_N) is A_(i₁)⋯A_(i_N); the most recently applied coefficient is the leftmost one. N=0 gives id_E, hence vanishing only for E=0. No integrability is required.
hypotheses: A commutative ringed Grothendieck site (C,J,O). E is finite locally free and Q is finite locally free, possibly Ω¹⊗T with T invertible. All maps, tensor powers and algebra objects are sheaves, with restriction-compatible local formulas.

θ:E→E⊗Q is O-linear. Integrability is required only for the symmetric-action comparison, not for the ordered-coordinate lemma. No characteristic, reducedness, basis or nilpotence condition is built into θ.
Local finite bases are used on trivializing covers; no tensor of global sections is identified with sections of a sheaf tensor.
proofSteps: Use the native affine arbitrary-N construction, unit boundary, exact ordered coefficient formula and finite-basis vanishing criterion. The established algebraic prototype treats all N≥0 without integrability and without a finite basis on E. Its comparison to the prescribed sheaf tensor powers and restriction/gluing still require E1.
Use the native/local finite tensor basis: its distinct ordered tuples give independent coefficients, with no symmetrization, factorial or exterior projection.
Dual basis contractions extract those coefficients. Conversely arbitrary local dual sections are linear combinations of dual basis sections, so multilinearity gives every ordered word.
Equality of the maps is local and therefore glues. For N=0 use the tensor unit and identity, rather than imposing a positive bound on this coordinate lemma.

nodes.title: Degree-one words generate Higgs augmentation powers
nodes.statement: For every N≥0, the Nth power of I=ker(ε) in S=Sym_A(V), V=Hom_A(Q,A), is the ideal span of the products ι(v₀)⋯ι(v_{N−1}) indexed by words Fin N→V. The empty word generates the whole ideal when N=0. The ideal is formed in the commutative source S, never in all of End_A(E).
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed.

V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative.
proofSteps: Use the built TauCeti.SymmetricAlgebra.augmentation_toIdeal_eq_span_range_ι. The built HopfIdeal.augmentation_toIdeal and SymmetricAlgebra.counitAlgHom_eq identify this with the kernel of the actual degree-zero augmentation algebraMapInv.
View Ideal.span in the commutative symmetric algebra as Submodule.span over S, and apply the built Submodule.span_pow. Its scalar-algebra and two-sidedness hypotheses hold in this commutative source.

Use the built Set.mem_pow to express membership in the Nth set power as a Fin N-indexed word of generators. Choose a preimage in V for each entry of range ι; List.map_ofFn identifies the resulting product. This includes N=0 and requires neither a basis nor a characteristic or rank assumption.
This is a Higgs-specific instantiation of built generic span and word facts. Do not add a new generic ideal-power induction, symmetric algebra carrier, or augmentation construction.

nodes.title: Augmentation powers and contraction words
nodes.statement: For every integer N≥0 and a generator-preserving action α:S→End_A(E), I^N⊆ker α iff every ordered product a(v₁)⋯a(v_N) is zero for all v₁,…,v_N∈V. Equivalently I^N annihilates E with its actual α-action. The exponent is the same on both sides; set-theoretic support on the zero section supplies no such exponent.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring; E and Q are A-modules. For this affine algebra no smoothness, characteristic-zero, reducedness, freeness or finite-generation assumption is imposed.

V=Hom_A(Q,A), S=Sym_A(V), ε:S→A is the canonical degree-zero augmentation, and I=ker ε. End_A(E) has its actual associative composition product and central A-algebra structure; it is not assumed commutative.
proofSteps: Apply augmentation_pow_generators, a Higgs-specific adapter of the built augmentation, span-power and set-word facts, for the same N≥0. No private generic power induction is needed.

Use the built Ideal.span_le and symmetricAction_word: containment in the source ideal ker α is equivalent to vanishing on every length-N generator word. End(E) is only an associative target; no commutative endomorphism-ring hypothesis is added.
The zero endomorphism acts by zero on every e, and equality of evaluations detects a zero endomorphism. At N=0 both criteria mean id_E=0, exactly when E is the zero module.

Keep I and ker α in S. An ambient left or two-sided ideal generated by the contractions in all End(E) can contain nonzero idempotents even when I² annihilates E; the concrete E12/E21 regression prevents this substitution.

nodes.statement: Given α:S→End_A(E), N≥0 and I^N⊆ker α, construct the unique A-algebra map β:S/I^N→End_A(E) satisfying β([s])=α(s). Such a generator-preserving factorization exists iff I^N⊆ker α. No radical quotient or unspecified larger nilpotence bound replaces I^N.

nodes.title: Symmetric projection loses ordered nilpotence
nodes.statement: Over k=F₂, take E=k[x,y]/(x²,y²), Q=kq₀⊕kq₁, and θ(e)=xe⊗q₀+ye⊗q₁. The two multiplication contractions commute and square to zero, but their product xy is nonzero. θ^[2](1)=xy⊗(q₀⊗q₁+q₁⊗q₀) is nonzero, whereas its image in E⊗Sym²(Q) is zero. In fact the projected second iterate is the zero map. The action has I²E≠0 and I³E=0. Thus symmetrized vanishing cannot replace ordered vanishing with the same exponent.
hypotheses: The ground field is F₂. E has the actual basis (1,x,y,xy), with x²=y²=0; Q has its actual two-element basis. No division by 2 is available.
proofSteps: Multiplication by x and y on the displayed four-dimensional module gives commuting matrices A,B with A²=B²=0 and AB=BA≠0.
The ordered degree-two tensor basis distinguishes q₀⊗q₁ and q₁⊗q₀, so their sum is nonzero. A dual tensor coefficient extracts xy from θ^[2](1).
In the symmetric quotient the two basis words agree, and 2=0. All diagonal coefficients also vanish, hence the projected map is zero.

All words of length three contain x² or y²; the mixed degree-two word acts nontrivially. Apply augmentation-power-words to get the exact bounds. The analogous finite regression over F₃ uses x³=y³=0: projected degree three vanishes while ordered degree three does not, and the ordered bound is five.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedStep_add
api.statement: S_(θ+η),n=S_θ,n+S_η,n.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedStep_contraction
api.statement: For any η:E→E⊗Q^⊗n, contract S_θ,n∘η by (v,vs) to obtain a_θ(v) times the vs contraction of η, in this order.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedStep_natural
api.statement: For every n≥0, S_psi,n composed with (f tensor u^(tensor n)) equals (f tensor u^(tensor(n+1))) composed with S_theta,n.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedStep.test_empty_coefficients

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedStep.test_scalar_nonzero

nodes.title: Native ordered Higgs iterates
nodes.statement: For every n≥0 construct θ^[n]:E→E⊗Q^⊗n recursively: θ^[0] is the inverse right tensor unit followed by the native identification R≅Q^⊗0; θ^[n+1]=S_θ,n∘θ^[n]. This definition uses no integrability or finite basis.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary commutative ring; E and Q are R-modules. No finite basis, field, reducedness or integrability is assumed on E or θ. A chosen finite basis of Q is required only in the coordinate and converse vanishing lemmas.

Use the native TensorPower R n Q, its degree-zero tensor unit and the actual associative composition algebra End_R(E). Products of endomorphisms are ordered from left to right, with the rightmost factor applied first. Scalars alone commute. These are affine module statements; E1 owns the global sheaf tensor-power and restriction/gluing interfaces.
proofSteps: Use primitive recursion into the native tensor-power codomains, with the actual degree-zero unit rather than a zero map.
Apply the successor step at each degree; its new factor is always the leftmost coefficient.
acceptance: For every n≥0 construct θ^[n]:E→E⊗Q^⊗n recursively: θ^[0] is the inverse right tensor unit followed by the native identification R≅Q^⊗0; θ^[n+1]=S_θ,n∘θ^[n]. This definition uses no integrability or finite basis.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_zero
api.statement: θ^[0](e)=e⊗1₀ in the actual degree-zero tensor unit.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_contraction
api.statement: Contraction by an ordered n-tuple of duals equals the ordered product of the n contractions of θ; at n=0 the product is id_E.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_zero_field
api.statement: The zero field has zero iterate at every positive order. Order zero remains the tensor-unit identity.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_natural
api.statement: For every n≥0, I_n(psi) composed with f equals (f tensor u^(tensor n)) composed with I_n(theta).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_mono
api.statement: If n≤m and I_n(theta)=0, then I_m(theta)=0, including n=0.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_zero_of_surjective
api.statement: For a surjective intertwiner f:E→F and any coefficient map u:Q→P, I_n(theta)=0 implies I_n(psi)=0 with exactly the same n.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_equiv_zero_iff
api.statement: For linear isomorphisms f:E≃F and u:Q≃P intertwining theta and psi, I_n(psi)=0 if and only if I_n(theta)=0, at the identical n.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_one
api.statement: Let a:Q≃Q^(tensor 1) be the existing inverse singleton tensor equivalence. Then I_1(theta)=(id_E tensor a) composed with theta.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_two
api.statement: Let a:Q≃Q^(tensor 1) be the inverse singleton equivalence and c=(a tensor a) followed by native tensor-power multiplication into Q^(tensor 2). Then I_2(theta)=(id_E tensor c) composed with affineOrderedSquare(theta).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_baseChange_zero
api.statement: For a finite basis b of Q and any n≥0, I_n(θ)=0 implies I_n(θ_S)=0 with exactly the same n, for every R-algebra S. E is arbitrary and S need not be flat.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_baseChange_zero_iff
api.statement: For a finite basis b of Q and faithfully flat R-algebra S, I_n(θ_S)=0 if and only if I_n(θ)=0, at the identical n≥0. E is an arbitrary R-module.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_natural_zero_iff_of_flat
api.statement: Let f:E→F and u:Q→P be injective R-linear maps with ψ∘f=(f⊗u)∘θ. If F,Q,P are flat over R, then for every n≥0, I_n(ψ)∘f=0 if and only if I_n(θ)=0. In particular a specified bound on ψ restricts to the same bound on θ. E need not be flat. The left side is the restriction along f, not vanishing on all of F.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_baseChange_comparison
api.statement: For every θ:E→E⊗_R Q and n≥0, D_n∘(I_n(θ))_S=I_n(θ_S) as actual S-linear maps E_S→E_S⊗_S Q_S^⊗n. Here (I_n(θ))_S is native scalar extension of the source-ring iterate, whereas I_n(θ_S) is formed recursively over S. No coefficient basis or integrability premise is required.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_baseChange_zero_of_arbitrary_coefficients
api.statement: For every specified n≥0 and every R-algebra S, I_n(θ)=0 implies I_n(θ_S)=0 at the identical n, for arbitrary R-modules E and Q. S need not be flat.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_baseChange_zero_iff_of_arbitrary_coefficients
api.statement: If S is faithfully flat over R, then for every specified n≥0, I_n(θ_S)=0 if and only if I_n(θ)=0, for arbitrary modules E and Q. The exponent is unchanged, and no flatness or finiteness of E or Q is needed.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_contraction_constant
api.statement: For n≥0 and v∈Q∨, contracting all n coefficient factors of I_n(θ) by v gives exactly a_θ(v)^n. At n=0 this is the tensor-unit identity, including the zero module.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_contractions_bound
api.statement: If I_N(θ)=0 for N≥0 then a_θ(v)^N=0 for every v∈Q∨. This implication holds for arbitrary Q without any dual-separation assumption; its converse is not asserted.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate_selected_word_zero
api.statement: If I_N(θ)=0 and a binary mask selects r≥N positions in a word of length n, the ordered θ product with identities at unselected positions is zero. Count selected occurrences, not distinct dual directions. Q may be arbitrary, and N=0 is retained under its genuine I_0=0 premise.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_unit_boundary
tests.statement: For any θ, contraction of θ^[0] by the empty tensor pairing is id_E, including E=0.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_zero
tests.statement: The zero field vanishes at all positive orders without imposing any assumption on E,Q.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_scalar_nonzero
tests.statement: For any nontrivial R, the scalar unit field on E=Q=R has nonzero θ^[n] for every n≥0.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_nonreduced_nilpotent
tests.statement: Over Z/4, θ=2 times the scalar unit field is nonzero but θ^[2]=0. This rules out unconditional rank-one or reduced-base shortcuts.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_natural_unit
tests.statement: For arbitrary fields theta,psi and maps f,u, the degree-zero naturality equation holds even without an intertwining assumption; the empty tensor word is mapped to itself.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_coefficient_quotient
tests.statement: For any u:Q→P and n, I_n(theta)=0 implies I_n((id_E tensor u) composed with theta)=0 at the same n.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_chart_identity
tests.statement: Take f=id_E,u=id_Q and psi=theta in the isomorphism transport theorem; the same-exponent equivalence holds for every n.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_bound_two_to_five
tests.statement: If I_2(theta)=0 then I_5(theta)=0 over any commutative ring, with no integrability assumption.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_one_zero_iff
tests.statement: For any theta, its first ordered iterate is zero if and only if theta itself is zero.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_two_zero_iff
tests.statement: For any theta, its second ordered iterate is zero if and only if the separate associator-defined ordered square is zero.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_characteristic_two_nonreflection
tests.statement: Over Z/2 with E=F=Q=P=Z/2, let theta(e)=e tensor 1, psi=0, f=id and u=0. The fields intertwine, I_1(psi)=0, and I_1(theta)≠0. Thus arbitrary coefficient maps cannot reflect a fixed bound even when f is an isomorphism.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_flat_subobject
tests.statement: For a horizontal pair of injections f:E→F and u:Q→P with F,Q,P flat, an ambient zero iterate I_n(ψ)=0 gives I_n(θ)=0; E is an arbitrary module.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_restriction_not_ambient
tests.statement: Over ℤ let f(a)=(a,0) and ψ(a,b)=(0,b)⊗1. Then ψ∘f=0 and ψ≠0. Restricted vanishing does not assert ambient vanishing, even with free finite modules and the identity coefficient map.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_arbitrary_coefficient_preservation
tests.statement: For R=ℤ, E=ℤ/4, Q=ℤ/2 and S=ℤ/2, I_n(θ)=0 implies I_n(θ_S)=0 for every specified n≥0 and actual θ. The extension S and both coefficient/source modules are not flat; no reflection is asserted.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_arbitrary_coefficient_reflection
tests.statement: For R=S=ℤ, E=ℤ/4 and Q=ℤ/2, I_n(θ_S)=0 iff I_n(θ)=0 at every specified n≥0 for every θ, using the faithfully flat identity algebra, without source or coefficient flatness.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_arbitrary_coefficient_degree_zero
tests.statement: If R is nontrivial and S is faithfully flat, the degree-zero receiving iterate of every θ:R→R⊗_R Q is nonzero, even for Q=0. Tensor nilpotence at exponent zero cannot mean the zero field.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_contraction_degree_zero
tests.statement: Contracting degree zero gives the identity endomorphism, not zero; this assertion includes the zero module.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineOrderedIterate.test_selected_repeated_direction
tests.statement: If I_2(θ)=0, the length-two word with both positions equal to v has zero product. Two selected occurrences count as two even though only one distinct dual direction occurs.

nodes.statement: For every n≥0, S_psi,n composed with (f tensor u^(tensor n)) equals (f tensor u^(tensor(n+1))) composed with S_theta,n.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring; E,F,Q,P are R-modules. Tensor powers mean the existing PiTensorProduct indexed by Fin n, including the degree-zero tensor unit. No basis, finiteness, integrability or reducedness is assumed.

The field has codomain E tensor Q. A successor prepends its new coefficient to the left of the previous word, while E remains the leftmost factor. For naturality assume psi composed with f equals (f tensor u) composed with theta. Surjectivity is used only for preservation on the whole target; reflection here uses isomorphisms for both f and u.
proofSteps: Reduce equality of linear maps by native tensor extensionality, then induction on the existing n-fold coefficient tensor.
For a pure coefficient word, substitute psi(f(e))=(f tensor u)(theta(e)); expand theta(e) by native tensor induction.
Both sides are f(x) tensor the word (u(q),u(q1),…,u(qn)); singleton, multiplication and degree-cast maps retain the new leftmost slot. Extend by scalar linearity and addition.
acceptance: The identity holds at n=0 with the actual empty tensor, not a zero surrogate.
Every linear coefficient map u is permitted, including u=0.
The convention retains the newly applied factor before the old ordered word.

nodes.title: Naturality at every ordered degree
nodes.statement: For every n≥0, I_n(psi) composed with f equals (f tensor u^(tensor n)) composed with I_n(theta).
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring; E,F,Q,P are R-modules. Tensor powers mean the existing PiTensorProduct indexed by Fin n, including the degree-zero tensor unit. No basis, finiteness, integrability or reducedness is assumed.

proofSteps: At n=0 both sides send e to f(e) tensor 1_0; the empty coefficient maps are equal by elimination of Fin 0.
At n+1 substitute the two successor recurrences and the degree-n induction hypothesis.
Apply step naturality and associativity of linear-map composition. No coefficient dualization or finite basis is required.

The same n appears on both sides; no enlargement of the exponent occurs.
In particular, coefficient specialization with f=id transports a vanishing iterate.

The zero increment is the hypothesis; each successor is S_theta,n+d composed with the zero map.
This is a statement about a given exponent; it does not construct a bound on an arbitrary infinite cover.

nodes.title: Reflect the same bound through two isomorphisms
nodes.statement: For linear isomorphisms f:E≃F and u:Q≃P intertwining theta and psi, I_n(psi)=0 if and only if I_n(theta)=0, at the identical n.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring; E,F,Q,P are R-modules. Tensor powers mean the existing PiTensorProduct indexed by Fin n, including the degree-zero tensor unit. No basis, finiteness, integrability or reducedness is assumed.

For naturality assume psi composed with f equals (f tensor u) composed with theta. Surjectivity is used only for preservation on the whole target; reflection here uses isomorphisms for both f and u.
proofSteps: The native tensor congruence of f and the family of n copies of u is an invertible linear map.
If I_n(psi)=0, naturality makes this invertible tensor map annihilate I_n(theta); injectivity reflects zero pointwise.
Conversely I_n(theta)=0 and surjectivity of f imply I_n(psi)=0. The proof covers n=0 without a separate positive-degree restriction.

Both module and coefficient isomorphisms are explicit; f=id with u=0 is a counterexample to omitting the latter.
There is no assumption that arbitrary scalar extension is faithful.

nodes.title: Scalar extension of an affine twisted field
nodes.statement: For θ:E→E⊗_R Q, construct the S-linear field θ_S:E_S→E_S⊗_S Q_S by the existing linear-map scalar extension followed by the existing tensor-distribution equivalence. On an elementary term a⊗(x⊗q), the latter gives (a⊗x)⊗(1⊗q). No coefficient differential map or integrability claim is included.

Tensor products, scalar extensions, bases and endomorphism composition use the existing native Mathlib carriers. No integrability, reducedness, field, flatness or finiteness premise is imposed unless separately stated.

Write E_S=S⊗_R E and Q_S=S⊗_R Q. A chosen basis b indexed by I is needed only for coordinate contraction/word comparisons; a finite index type I is required only for the all-order vanishing criterion. E remains an arbitrary module. A successor prepends its coefficient on the left, and the rightmost endomorphism acts first. At n=0 the ordered product is the identity.
proofSteps: Compose the native scalar extension of θ with the native S-linear tensor equivalence; introduce no new generic tensor or scalar-extension carrier.

Write T(θ,ψ)=rightComm∘(θ⊗id_F)+assoc⁻¹∘(id_E⊗ψ), with target (E⊗_R F)⊗_R Q; write a_θ(v)=rid∘(id_E⊗v)∘θ and κ(θ)=(id_E⊗π₂)∘I₂(θ) for the inherited native contraction and exterior square. Tensor associators, symmetry and unitors are the existing Mathlib linear equivalences, not new general module constructions.

Only the integrability theorem requires a chosen finite basis b:I→Q. Every other new tensor identity holds for arbitrary Q. The tensor unit carries the zero Higgs field. This is the affine λ=0 specialization: neither the nonzero-parameter Leibniz balancing nor actual sheaf restriction/gluing is discharged.
proofSteps: Compose the native tensor maps with rightComm and the inverse associator, then add in the native module of linear maps.
acceptance: Construct T(θ,ψ):E⊗_R F→(E⊗_R F)⊗_R Q as the sum rightComm∘(θ⊗id_F)+assoc⁻¹∘(id_E⊗ψ). Both summands retain one common coefficient module Q; no tensor-square coefficient or division is introduced.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_tmul
api.statement: For every e∈E and f∈F, T(θ,ψ)(e⊗f)=rightComm(θ(e)⊗f)+assoc⁻¹(e⊗ψ(f)).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_zero
api.statement: T(0_E,0_F)=0 as a native linear map E⊗_R F→(E⊗_R F)⊗_R Q.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions
api.statement: For every v∈Hom_R(Q,R), a_T(θ,ψ)(v)=a_θ(v)⊗id_F+id_E⊗a_ψ(v) in End_R(E⊗_R F).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_commute
api.statement: For v,w∈Hom_R(Q,R), if a_θ(v)a_θ(w)=a_θ(w)a_θ(v) and a_ψ(v)a_ψ(w)=a_ψ(w)a_ψ(v), then a_T(θ,ψ)(v)a_T(θ,ψ)(w)=a_T(θ,ψ)(w)a_T(θ,ψ)(v). Products are composition with the right factor applied first.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_integrable
api.statement: If Q has a chosen finite basis b:I→Q and κ(θ)=κ(ψ)=0, then κ(T(θ,ψ))=0. E and F remain arbitrary R-modules, including torsion modules.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_coefficientMap
api.statement: For any R-linear u:Q→P, (id_(E⊗F)⊗u)∘T(θ,ψ)=T((id_E⊗u)∘θ,(id_F⊗u)∘ψ). This is same-ring postcomposition, with no injectivity or flatness requirement on u.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_horizontal
api.statement: For fields θ′ on E′ and ψ′ on F′ with coefficients Q and R-linear f:E→E′, g:F→F′, suppose θ′∘f=(f⊗id_Q)∘θ and ψ′∘g=(g⊗id_Q)∘ψ. Then T(θ′,ψ′)∘(f⊗g)=((f⊗g)⊗id_Q)∘T(θ,ψ). No map needs to be invertible.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_comm
api.statement: For the native symmetry c:E⊗_R F≃F⊗_R E, T(ψ,θ)∘c=(c⊗id_Q)∘T(θ,ψ).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_rid
api.statement: For the native right unitor ρ:E⊗_R R≃E and the zero field on R, θ∘ρ=(ρ⊗id_Q)∘T(θ,0_R).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_lid
api.statement: For the native left unitor ℓ:R⊗_R E≃E and the zero field on R, θ∘ℓ=(ℓ⊗id_Q)∘T(0_R,θ).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_assoc
api.statement: For a third arbitrary R-module G with field χ:G→G⊗_R Q and the native associator α:(E⊗_R F)⊗_R G≃E⊗_R(F⊗_R G), T(θ,T(ψ,χ))∘α=(α⊗id_Q)∘T(T(θ,ψ),χ).

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_separate_commute
api.statement: For every dual direction v, a_θ(v)⊗id_F commutes with id_E⊗a_ψ(v) in End_R(E⊗_R F). These operators act on different factors even when contractions within a factor do not commute.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_pow
api.statement: For all k≥0 and v∈Q∨, a_T(v)^k=Σ_{i=0}^k binom(k,i)·TensorProduct.map(a_θ(v)^i,a_ψ(v)^(k−i)), as an equality of native endomorphisms. The coefficient acts by repeated addition.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_bound
api.statement: For N,M≥0 and v∈Q∨, if a_θ(v)^N=0 and a_ψ(v)^M=0 then a_T(v)^(N+M−1)=0. The zero-exponent hypotheses, when possible, are retained rather than silently excluded.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_bound_of_le
api.statement: For N,M,k≥0 with N+M≤k+1, vanishing of a_θ(v)^N and a_ψ(v)^M implies a_T(v)^k=0.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_isNilpotent
api.statement: If a_θ(v) and a_ψ(v) are nilpotent endomorphisms, then a_T(v) is nilpotent; witnesses N,M produce the explicit witness N+M−1. No claim is made about a common bound as v varies.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_uniform_bound
api.statement: If a_θ(v)^N=0 and a_ψ(v)^M=0 for every v∈Q∨, then a_T(v)^(N+M−1)=0 for every v. Uniform vanishing of these self-powers alone is not the full ordered nilpotence criterion.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_bound_of_ordered
api.statement: For N,M≥0, if I_N(θ)=0 and I_M(ψ)=0 then, for every v∈Q∨, a_T(v)^(N+M−1)=0. This is an actual affine consequence of ordered factor bounds; it does not establish I_(N+M−1)(T)=0.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_cross_commute
api.statement: For all v,w∈Q∨, Lθ(v)=aθ(v)⊗id_F commutes with Rψ(w)=id_E⊗aψ(w). There is no requirement that v=w or that contractions within either factor commute.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_selected_word
api.statement: For n≥0, vs:Fin n→Q∨ and c:Fin n→Bool, the ordered product choosing Lθ(vs(i)) when c(i)=true and Rψ(vs(i)) otherwise is TensorProduct.map of the ordered E and F products, inserting the identity at every unchosen position. The within-factor order is unchanged.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_word_expansion
api.statement: For n≥0 and arbitrary vs:Fin n→Q∨, the ordered product of aT(vs(i)) equals the sum over all binary masks c:Fin n→Bool of TensorProduct.map(Pθ(c),Pψ(not c)), where Pθ/Pψ are the ordered contraction products with identities at unchosen positions. The sum has 2^n terms with their full multiplicity; no division or within-factor commutation is used.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_word_summand_zero
api.statement: For positive N,M, n with N+M≤n+1, and actual bounds I_N(θ)=I_M(ψ)=0, each binary-mask summand TensorProduct.map(Pθ(c),Pψ(not c)) is zero for every mixed dual word of length n.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_contractions_word_zero
api.statement: For positive N,M and n with N+M≤n+1, I_N(θ)=I_M(ψ)=0 implies every ordered mixed dual contraction word of T(θ,ψ) of length n is zero. This holds for arbitrary Q; it does not assert that Q's dual detects the tensor-valued iterate.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_bound_of_basis
api.statement: For a chosen finite basis b:I→Q and positive N,M, I_N(θ)=I_M(ψ)=0 implies I_(N+M−1)(T(θ,ψ))=0 as an equality of actual native tensor-valued linear maps. E,F need no basis, finiteness or flatness, and the fields need not be integrable.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_bound_of_basis_of_le
api.statement: Under the same finite coefficient basis and positive factor bounds, every k with N+M≤k+1 satisfies I_k(T(θ,ψ))=0. The specified exponent is preserved rather than replaced by an unspecified existence assertion.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_bound_of_basis_baseChange
api.statement: For every R-algebra S, a finite coefficient basis over R and positive ordered factor bounds N,M imply I_(N+M−1)(T(S⊗θ,S⊗ψ))=0 over S. No flatness, faithful-flatness or characteristic condition on S is required for this preservation direction.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_bound_of_split_basis
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Let P have a finite R-basis and let u:Q→P, v:P→Q satisfy vu=id_Q. For positive N,M with I_N(θ)=0 and I_M(ψ)=0, I_{N+M−1}(T)=0.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_bound_of_projective
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. For positive N,M with I_N(θ)=0 and I_M(ψ)=0, I_{N+M−1}(T)=0.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_larger_bound_of_projective
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. For positive N,M, k with N+M≤k+1 and I_N(θ)=I_M(ψ)=0, I_k(T)=0.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_nilpotent_of_projective
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. If θ and ψ each have a positive zero ordered iterate, then T has a positive zero ordered iterate.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_baseChange_of_projective
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. For any commutative R-algebra S, positive N,M and I_N(θ)=I_M(ψ)=0, the tensor of the actual scalar-extended fields has zero ordered iterate N+M−1. No flatness or faithfulness of S is required for preservation.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_chart_of_projective
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. For any commutative R-algebra S, S-linear equivalences e:S⊗_R(E⊗_R F)≃G and q:S⊗_R Q≃P, and positive bounds N,M on θ,ψ, the actual chart field transported by e,q has zero ordered iterate N+M−1.

api.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField_ordered_principalCover_of_projective
api.statement: Let R be any commutative ring, E,F,Q be R-modules and θ:E→E⊗_R Q, ψ:F→F⊗_R Q be actual R-linear fields. Use the inherited ordered iterate I_n, with ordered tensor-power coefficient target and the prescribed tensor field T=θ⊗1+1⊗ψ. Let s⊆R satisfy span(s)=R, and for each r∈s let A_r be an actual localization away from r. Assume A_r⊗_R Q is finitely generated projective and that the scalar-extended fields have positive fixed zero degrees N,M on every r. Then I_{N+M−1}(T)=0 over R. Q need not have a global basis, and its global projectivity is not a premise.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_zero
tests.statement: For arbitrary E,F,Q, tensoring the two zero Higgs fields gives the zero field.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_integer_sum
tests.statement: Over R=ℤ and E=F=Q=ℤ, tensor the two fields e↦e⊗1. The value at 1⊗1 is (1⊗1)⊗2, retaining both summands.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_char_two_cancellation
tests.statement: Over R=E=F=Q=ZMod 2, the scalar unit field e↦e⊗1 is nonzero, but tensoring it with itself gives the zero field. Tensor-field vanishing cannot reflect the vanishing of either input.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_torsion_integrability
tests.statement: Over ℤ with Q=ℤ, use E=ZMod 2 and F=ZMod 4 and the one-direction fields with identity operators and direction 1. Their tensor field has zero native exterior square, without a flatness or freeness assumption on either module.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_zero_direction_map
tests.statement: For arbitrary fields θ,ψ and an arbitrary target coefficient module P, postcompose both fields by the zero map Q→P; their tensor field is zero.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_contracted_binomial
tests.statement: The k-fold self-contraction of the actual tensor field is the integral binomial sum for every k≥0, including the tensor-unit boundary.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_ordered_to_contracted
tests.statement: Arbitrary-module factor ordered bounds N,M give the specified tensor contraction bound N+M−1 in each chosen dual direction.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_bound_one
tests.statement: Two vanishing contractions have vanishing tensor contraction, the N=M=1 boundary.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_larger_bound
tests.statement: Factor contraction squares zero imply the fifth power of the tensor contraction is zero via the exact larger-exponent inequality.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_integer_sharp_bound
tests.statement: Over ℤ let J(x,y)=(y,0) and θ=J⊗1. The self-contraction of T(θ,θ) has cube zero and square nonzero, detected at (0,1)⊗(0,1) by the first-coordinate pairing giving 2. Replacing N+M−1 by max(N,M) is false.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_char_two_square_cancellation
tests.statement: For the same J and θ over ZMod 2, the tensor self-contraction square is zero because its two equal mixed terms cancel. The proof uses actual tensor maps and no division by 2.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_self_powers_do_not_detect_ordered
tests.statement: Over K=ZMod 2 let V=K², J(x,y)=(y,0), E=V⊗V, Q=K² and θ=(J⊗id)⊗(1,0)+(id⊗J)⊗(0,1). Every dual contraction square vanishes, but I₂(θ) is nonzero: the mixed ordered contraction (first coordinate, second coordinate) is J⊗J, detected as 1 on (0,1)⊗(0,1). No equivalence between self-power vanishing and ordered nilpotence is asserted.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_word_empty
tests.statement: The n=0 tensor contraction word is the identity on E⊗F, not zero; the binary-mask sum has one identity summand.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_word_two
tests.statement: For arbitrary v,w the length-two word is map(aθ(v)aθ(w),1)+map(aθ(v),aψ(w))+map(aθ(w),aψ(v))+map(1,aψ(v)aψ(w)). The E/F subsequences retain their order even for noncommuting directions.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_bound_zero_factor
tests.statement: For a finite coefficient basis, M>0 and I_M(ψ)=0, I_M(T(0,ψ))=0. The bound with N=1 preserves exactly M rather than adding an unnecessary exponent.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_empty_coefficients
tests.statement: If Q is the zero module, every θ,ψ has I_1(T(θ,ψ))=0. Degree zero still gives the tensor-unit map.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_char_two_bound
tests.statement: Over K=ZMod 2, V=K×K and J(x,y)=(y,0), let θ=J⊗(1,0) and ψ=J⊗(0,1). Each has ordered bound 2, while their actual tensor field has I_3=0 and I_2≠0. Distinct mixed directions remain nonzero although all self-contraction squares vanish.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_integer_bound
tests.statement: Over ℤ with V=ℤ×ℤ and J(x,y)=(y,0), θ=J⊗1 has I_2=0; the actual tensor field T(θ,θ) has I_3=0 and I_2≠0. The integer mixed coefficient is 2(J⊗J), so max(2,2) is not the tensor bound.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_mixed_nonflat_baseChange
tests.statement: Over ℤ with a finite coefficient basis and I_2(θ)=I_2(ψ)=0, the tensor of the two scalar-extended fields over ZMod 2 has actual ordered bound 3. This preservation uses no flatness.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_split_basis_bound
tests.statement: A specified coefficient retract of a finite-basis P transfers the two order2 bounds to order3, without a basis of Q.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_bound
tests.statement: Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. Two order2 bounds imply order3 for T.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_zero_fields
tests.statement: Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. For θ=ψ=0 the tensor field has zero order1 iterate.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_larger_bound
tests.statement: Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. Two order2 bounds imply the specified larger order5 bound.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_positive_nilpotence
tests.statement: Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. Two positive ordered nilpotence witnesses give a positive tensor witness.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_nonflat_baseChange
tests.statement: Over ℤ with finite-projective Q, two order2 bounds remain order3 after scalar extension to ZMod2, a nonflat scalar extension.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_chart_bound
tests.statement: Assume Q is finitely generated and projective. No basis of Q and no finiteness, projectivity or flatness of E or F are required. No integrability, characteristic or reducedness assumption is used. The two order2 bounds give order3 in any actual scalar-extended module chart, with the stated coefficient and field-module equivalences.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_principal_cover
tests.statement: On a principal cover spanning1, local finite-projective coefficient modules and two local order2 bounds detect the global order3 tensor-valued bound.

tests.name: TwistedHiggsBundle.affineTensorField.test_projective_nonfree_corner
tests.statement: Let R=ℚ×ℚ and Q=ℚ with the first-projection action. The real maps u(x)=(x,0) and v(a,b)=a split Q off R, making it finite projective. The nonzero scalar (0,1) annihilates1. Two actual order2 field bounds still imply order3. Q is nonzero and cannot be a globally free R-module since it has a nonzero annihilator.

hypotheses: R is an arbitrary commutative ring; E,F,Q are arbitrary R-modules. θ:E→E⊗_R Q and ψ:F→F⊗_R Q are actual linear fields. No integrability, characteristic, reducedness, basis, flatness or finiteness assumption is used.

Write a_θ(v)=rid∘(id_E⊗v)∘θ, T(θ,ψ) for the inherited actual affine tensor field, and I_n(θ) for the ordered iterate with its native associators. Products in End are composition with the right factor applied first; natural scalar multiplication repeats addition and never divides by binomial coefficients.

Every conclusion concerns contraction powers, not vanishing of the whole tensor-valued ordered iterate. Repeated self-contractions do not detect all mixed ordered words in characteristic two. The sheaf tensor/restriction/descent comparison remains with E1.
proofSteps: Use the existing arbitrary ordered-word contraction formula with the constant tuple of v. List.ofFn_const changes the word to n repeated copies; its product is the native endomorphism power.
acceptance: For n≥0 and v∈Q∨, contracting all n coefficient factors of I_n(θ) by v gives exactly a_θ(v)^n. At n=0 this is the tensor-unit identity, including the zero module.

proofSteps: Regard the products as compositions of native linear maps. Both Lθ(v)Rψ(w) and Rψ(w)Lθ(v) equal TensorProduct.map(aθ(v),aψ(w)) by the two existing tensor-composition identities.

nodes.title: Biadditive tensor parameter operator
nodes.statement: For D∈Preconnection(Ω,λ,E), C∈Preconnection(Ω,λ,F), construct the actual biadditive B:E→(F→(E⊗_R F)⊗_R W), B(e,f)=ρ(D(e)⊗f)+α⁻¹(e⊗C(f)), where ρ:(E⊗W)⊗F≃(E⊗F)⊗W is the native right commutor and α:(E⊗F)⊗W≃E⊗(F⊗W) is the native associator.
hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra; Ω is the existing intrinsic degree-zero/one/two calculus TwoForms, with actual derivation d₀:R→W, additive d₁:W→Z and alternating R-bilinear wedge satisfying its defining equations.

E,F,W,Z are genuine R-modules with additive commutative groups; W also has its specified k-module structure. λ is the same element of R on both preconnections. No basis, finite generation, projectivity, flatness, smoothness, characteristic or field hypothesis is used.

D:E→E⊗_R W and C:F→F⊗_R W are the actual additive section maps with λ-Leibniz equations. d₀λ=0 and integrability are not needed for the raw preconnection tensor; they remain requirements for later curvature and flat-bundle results.
proofSteps: Use the two actual additive maps and native tensor maps to define the displayed sum.

acceptance: Use the genuine additive carrier and actual tensor associator, right commutor, map and symmetry. Neither summand is required to be R-linear.

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_horizontal
api.statement: For actual R-linear u:E→E′,v:F→F′ and common-λ preconnections D,C,D′,C′ with D′u=(u⊗id_W)D and C′v=(v⊗id_W)C, their native tensor map is horizontal: affineTensor(D′,C′)((u⊗v)x)=((u⊗v)⊗id_W)affineTensor(D,C)(x), for every x∈E⊗_R F.

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_comm
api.statement: For the actual native symmetry τ:E⊗_R F≃F⊗_R E, affineTensor(C,D)(τx)=(τ⊗id_W)affineTensor(D,C)(x) for every x∈E⊗_R F.

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_assoc
api.statement: For common-λ preconnections D on E, C on F and B on G, let T_L=(D⊗C)⊗B and T_R=D⊗(C⊗B), using the actual affineTensor. The native α:(E⊗_R F)⊗_R G≃E⊗_R(F⊗_R G) is horizontal: T_R(αx)=(α⊗id_W)T_L(x) for every x.

api.name: Preconnection.horizontal_symm
api.statement: Let D on E and C on F be common-λ preconnections and u:E≃ₗ[R]F an actual linear equivalence. If C(u(e))=(u⊗id_W)D(e) for every e, then D(u⁻¹(f))=(u⁻¹⊗id_W)C(f) for every f. The inverse is the native inverse of u, with no extra horizontal-inverse hypothesis.

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_assoc_symm
api.statement: With T_L,T_R and α as above, T_L(α⁻¹x)=(α⁻¹⊗id_W)T_R(x) for every x∈E⊗_R(F⊗_R G). Thus both directions of the native associator intertwine the actual additive tensor preconnections.

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_lid
api.statement: Write U_λ for the existing actual unit preconnection on R, U_λ(a)=λ(1⊗d₀a). For every common-λ D on E, the native left unitor ℓ:R⊗_R E≃E is horizontal: D(ℓx)=(ℓ⊗id_W)(U_λ⊗D)(x) for all x. In particular, on a⊗e the normalized value is aD(e)+λ(e⊗d₀a).

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_rid
api.statement: For D on E and U_λ(a)=λ(1⊗d₀a), the native right unitor r:E⊗_R R≃E is horizontal: D(rx)=(r⊗id_W)(D⊗U_λ)(x) for every x. On e⊗a its normalized value is aD(e)+λ(e⊗d₀a).

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_lid_symm
api.statement: The inverse left unitor is horizontal: (U_λ⊗D)(ℓ⁻¹e)=(ℓ⁻¹⊗id_W)D(e). Since the native inverse is ℓ⁻¹e=1⊗e, inserting the unit preserves the full coefficient tensor D(e).

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_rid_symm
api.statement: The inverse right unitor is horizontal: (D⊗U_λ)(r⁻¹e)=(r⁻¹⊗id_W)D(e). The native inverse r⁻¹e=e⊗1 therefore preserves the full coefficient tensor D(e).

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_extend_left

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_extend_right
api.statement: For T=D⊗_λ C and y∈F⊗W, T₁(a_W⁻¹(e⊗y))=a_Z⁻¹(e⊗C₁(y))+tensorWedge(D(e)⊗y).

api.name: Preconnection.affineTensor_curvature_tmul

hypotheses: k and R are commutative rings and R is a k-algebra. E,F,G,W,Z are native R-modules with additive commutative groups; W has its specified compatible k-module structure and IsScalarTower k R W. No field, smoothness, characteristic, finite generation, basis, projectivity or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

The existing TwoForms input Ω has d₀:Derivation k R W, additive d₁:W→Z and alternating R-bilinear wedge, with d₁(aω)=d₀a∧ω+a d₁ω and d₁d₀=0. It is supplied calculus, not a construction of universal sheaf forms.

D:E→E⊗W and C:F→F⊗W are actual additive preconnections with the same parameter λ and the λ-Leibniz equation. Horizontal u means C(u(e))=(u⊗id_W)(D(e)). The coordinate transport uses an actual R-linear equivalence u:E≃F, without differentiating u as an R-linear connection map.

λ is arbitrary for the additive extension, curvature and coordinate-transport identities. The curvatureLinear construction and its six APIs require the explicit equation d₀λ=0. The global reserved key remains finite locally free on a ringed differential site with relatively constant λ.
proofSteps: Unfold the actual additive composition in transport.
acceptance: Retain actual native tensor carriers, the unchanged parameter and every derivative correction; do not assume an additive preconnection or extension is R-linear.
The native certificate proves these affine equations. Global sheaf construction, arbitrary ring changes and source correspondences remain separate open obligations.
